title: The Rosewood Parlor
subtitle: A peaceful manor interrupted by poison
description: Lord Reginald Rosewood was found dead in the estate conservatory before evening tea. Five guests and staff were scattered across the manor's east wing. Deduce everyone's location and discover who was alone with Lord Reginald.

characters.name: Lord Reginald
characters.description: The wealthy master of Rosewood Manor.

characters.name: Clara Mercer
characters.description: An avid collector of rare literature.

characters.name: Dr. Julian Sterling
characters.description: The family physician visiting for the weekend.

clues.text: Lord Reginald was seated at row 1, column 2 near the garden doors.
Evelyn was standing directly beside Lord Reginald.
Dr. Julian Sterling was in the billiard room.
Julian was entirely alone in his room.
Julian was standing directly beside the billiard table.
Arthur Vance was in the library.
Arthur was inspecting the antique globe.
Clara was browsing books in the library with Arthur.
Clara stood right beside the oak bookshelf.
Beatrice was warming herself by the parlor fireplace.

resolution: Evelyn Rosewood was the only person in the conservatory with Lord Reginald. Julian had the billiard room to himself, Arthur and Clara were browsing the library, and Beatrice was tending the parlor fire. Her ambition for the estate gives the story its motive, but it was the placements that proved she was alone with him.

deductions.text: Lord Reginald is fixed at row 1, column 2 in the conservatory.
Evelyn must share an edge with him. The stone fountain blocks the cell below him, leaving row 1, column 1 or row 1, column 3. Only the first is in column 1.
Julian is in the billiard room beside the billiard table. Its only open neighbour in row 4 is row 4, column 2, and he has the room to himself.
Arthur is in the library beside the antique globe. The globe’s neighbour in column 4 is row 2, column 4.
Clara joins Arthur in the library beside the oak bookshelf. The bookshelf’s open neighbours are row 1, column 5 and row 2, column 6; only the first is in row 1.
Beatrice stands beside the parlor fireplace in column 5, which leaves row 5, column 5.
With everyone placed, Evelyn is the only suspect sharing the conservatory with Lord Reginald.

helpPrompts.text: Begin with the clue that fixes someone to an exact cell. Everything else can be built around that person.
A “beside” clue allows only the open cells directly above, below, left, or right. Diagonals never count, and object cells are blocked.
For each person, combine their “beside” clue with their row or column clue. Which cells satisfy both?
Clara is in the same room as Arthur. Settle Arthur first, then use Clara’s other clues inside that room.
When everyone is placed, look at the victim’s room. Which suspect is the only one sharing it?

tutorial.title: Pick a person
tutorial.text: Tap a portrait under Persons of Interest to select someone. You can also drag a portrait straight onto the map.

tutorial.title: Place them on the map
tutorial.text: With someone selected, tap an open cell. Rows count from the top and columns from the left, both starting at 1. Tap another cell to move them; nothing is checked until you ask.

tutorial.title: “Beside” means sharing an edge
tutorial.text: A person beside someone or something is directly above, below, left, or right of it. Diagonal cells never count.

tutorial.title: Objects block cells
tutorial.text: Furniture such as the stone fountain fills its cell, so nobody can stand there. Use that to rule out neighbours quickly.

tutorial.title: Take notes
tutorial.text: Switch to Exclude Note, select a person, and tap a cell where they cannot be. Notes are only for you; they never affect checking.

tutorial.title: Tick off clues
tutorial.text: Tap a clue to mark it as used. When everyone is placed, press Check Solution.
